5 Small Apartment Storage Mistakes Costing You Valuable Space

By Sarah Mitchell · 4 min read · Updated August 10, 2026

Does your small apartment constantly feel cluttered and cramped, no matter how much you tidy up? The issue usually isn't the size of your apartment, but rather a few common storage mistakes that are secretly eating up your square footage.

Here are 5 common small apartment storage mistakes that are costing you valuable space, and how to fix them immediately.

Storing Things on the Floor

The fastest way to make a room feel tiny is to eat away at the visible floor space. Baskets, shoes, and boxes resting on the floor visually shrink the room.

The fix: Never store anything on the floor if it can be elevated. Use wall hooks, floating shelves, or store items inside hidden furniture like an ottoman bench.

Ignoring the Back of Doors

Your doors are massive, blank canvases of storage potential. Leaving them empty is a huge missed opportunity in a tight space.

The fix: Utilize an over-the-door hanging organizer to store pantry items, cleaning supplies, or toiletries without using any floor or shelf space.

Over-the-Door Hanging Organizer

Problem: Crowded cabinets and lack of pantry or bathroom storage.
Solution: A high-capacity hanging organizer with multiple sturdy pockets that turns any door into a storage wall.

  • Large capacity pockets hold heavy bottles
  • Clear windows to easily see contents
  • Requires zero tools or drilling to install
Check Price on Amazon →

Wasting Under-Bed Space

Many renters just push dust bunnies under their bed. This area is equivalent to a large dresser and should never be left empty.

The fix: Invest in low-profile under-bed storage containers to house out-of-season clothing, extra bedding, and shoes.

Not Compressing Bulky Items

Folding a thick winter duvet and placing it on a closet shelf can take up the entire rack. Bulky items contain mostly trapped air.

The fix: Use vacuum storage bags to shrink soft, bulky items down by 80%, instantly tripling your closet capacity.

Vacuum Storage Bags

Problem: Bulky winter bedding taking over the entire closet.
Solution: High-compression vacuum bags that shrink your blankets and sweaters to create 80% more space.

  • Includes a hand pump for easy travel use
  • Double-zip seal prevents air leakage
  • Protects items from dust and moisture
Check Price on Amazon →

Cluttered Coffee Tables and Nightstands

When flat surfaces are covered in remotes, mail, and books, the whole room feels messy.

The fix: Give these small items a dedicated home. Use a sofa arm organizer for your living room remotes, and a bedside caddy for your nighttime reading.

By avoiding these 5 mistakes, you can reclaim your apartment's space and create a calming, clutter-free environment.
